### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **69** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-hook-dispatch.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d833b50fbb64ae3f0c83607cfdcaaefd260db77`.

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-hook-dispatch.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d833b50fbb64ae3f0c83607cfdcaaefd260db77` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7dc027acd3cdf310c971678266c8f4e34da97ec7` — the merge of head `30f5259bc6e7fa7657838f5d7cff85e7b5996f19` into base `6d833b50fbb64ae3f0c83607cfdcaaefd260db77`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7dc027acd3cdf310c971678266c8f4e34da97ec7 && git checkout 7dc027acd3cdf310c971678266c8f4e34da97ec7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6d833b50fbb64ae3f0c83607cfdcaaefd260db77 30f5259bc6e7fa7657838f5d7cff85e7b5996f19 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6d833b50fbb64ae3f0c83607cfdcaaefd260db77 && git merge --no-ff 30f5259bc6e7fa7657838f5d7cff85e7b5996f19

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d833b50fbb64ae3f0c83607cfdcaaefd260db77
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6d833b50fbb64ae3f0c83607cfdcaaefd260db77` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Test Core (7/10): the re-run failed again. Measured: not this PR** (2026-11-19T09:04Z)

The re-run (attempt 2) timed out on the same file, `plugin-security` `org-admin-assignment-boundary.posture.test.ts:1153` (posture 'isolated': auditorDelegate and orgAdminAuditor, 5000 ms). A second failure is treated as real, so it was measured (dev addendum 7004581195 on #35167):

- **Code path.** Instrumented, not committed: the file makes 3866 inserts and 484 deletes, and on this branch the after-abort unit opens **0** times, exactly as on main. When `ownUnit` is false, the write takes the same executor, with no added await, unit, retry or timer.
- **Interleaved A/B, 3 runs per tree, swapping only the two engine files.** Test time: main 21.03 / 20.61 / 19.21 s, branch 20.09 / 19.76 / 19.31 s. Isolated auditorDelegate: main 528 / 557 / 518 ms, branch 558 / 560 / 522 ms.
- **Other CI runs today, none of which contain this change:** main scheduled run 44484542279 took 645.59 s for the package, with the case at 3217 ms. PR #35383 run 44480050457, on the same shard partners, took 751.67 s, with the case at **4705 ms**. PR #35387 took 654.87 s, with the case at 3136 ms. Light shards took about 430 s. This PR took 926 s and then 769 s.

The case reaches 4.5–4.7 s without this change whenever the shard is loaded. The fix belongs to the test's time budget, not to this diff. Follow-up card: see the next comment on #35167. No timeout is raised in this PR and no test is skipped.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：给对象绑了写数据的前置钩子或会拦截的后置钩子后，新增和删除在单连接数据库（SQLite）上不再让别人的写入排队等权限检查；新增、修改、删除三个动作的事务边界成为同一条规则。
- 为什么做：这是你选的"三个动作一条规则"，修改已经先做完，这一单补齐新增和删除。
- 出错会怎样：只影响绑了这类钩子的对象；钩子报错时整笔写入照样回滚。中间件在写入完成之后才做的收尾工作，不再和这一行一起回滚，和没绑钩子的对象一样。
- 要你做什么：无。区域自行落地。

## 席位核对

**L1-a: ACCEPT** · head `30f5259bc6e7fa7657838f5d7cff85e7b5996f19` · Fixes #35167 · 2026-11-19T11:19Z

**Scope of this record.** The relay asked for a merge-only delta over an earlier verdict on `155c9e54ec`. No L1 record exists on this PR or on #35167; the comments are the docs-drift bot and two seat CI judgments, 7003622533 and 7004622123. So this record is a full L1 of the PR's own diff at `155c9e54ec`, plus the merge delta.

**Merge delta.** `30f5259bc6` = merge of main `6d833b50fb` into `155c9e54ec`. The PR's own diff is byte-identical before and after the merge, checked by `diff` of `git diff merge-base..155c9e54ec` against `git diff M^2..M`. It is main-only, and it brings in #35452, the posture-test split that cleared the Test Core timeout. K=3; `merge-tree` against main clean; CI 37 success / 16 skipped / 0 failed. Trailers are model-free.

**Code (9 files, +408/−36).**
- `insert` and `delete` drop their door re-entry, `return this.inAfterAbortUnit(() => this.insert|delete(…))`. Each now computes `ownUnit` once and wraps only the executor handed to `executeWithMiddleware`. This is the same `inOwnUnit` shape `update` already ships (`engine-update.ts:172-175, :475`, #35142), so the three verbs read one rule.
- `inAfterAbortUnit` is unchanged. It runs `write` under `this.transaction(…)`, and the body reaches the unit's transaction through the same ambient path the old re-entry relied on, since that re-entry also passed the caller's `options` through unchanged.
- Between the door and the executor nothing writes. The calls there are `assertWriteAllowed`, the organization-probe drop, `enforceTransactionOrigin` on the caller's own transaction, `withResolvedWhere` (a read), and `claimReferentialCascadeDelete`, an in-memory token. The claim's docblock is corrected to match: no `delete()` re-enters itself now, so the claiming call is the dispatching call.
- The `Pick<>` lists lose `'insert'` and `'delete'`, confirming no self-call is left. The durability-census resolution control moves from the gone `this.delete(…)` to `insertMany`'s `this.insert(…)`, with the same shape and a reason that says why.

**Pins.** `plugin-security/src/{insert,delete}-unit-inside-middleware-sqlite.test.ts`:
- per hook kind, a second writer lands while the first is parked in the middleware chain;
- CONTROL: an `after*` that throws still leaves no row (insert) or keeps the row (delete) on SQLite.

Ablation per verb, with the engine file restored from base: 2 failed / 2 passed, the hooked cells "still waiting", and the controls green throughout. objectql 13878 tests pass.

**Declaration: agreed.** `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` / `@objectstack/objectql` patch. Nothing is refused and no authorable key moves. The one observable shift is a middleware's post-`next()` work running after the commit on a hooked object. The changeset states it, and it matches what every unhooked object and `update` already do, the same declaration #35142 shipped under.

**Routing.** Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 35386`), no contract face: data-1 lands it. A new push needs a fresh L1 only if it changes more than a main merge.
